hook_text: South Africa grows enough food to feed everyone, so why do so many children still go to bed hungry?
clip_script: South Africa's farms produce enough food for all of us. We even export oranges, grapes and wine around the world. And yet about one in five households sometimes doesn't have enough to eat. Roughly a quarter of young children are shorter than they should be, because of poor nutrition. The problem isn't the food on the shelves. It's the money in people's pockets. That's what food security is about: everyone, every day, able to get enough safe, healthy food. Science has helped grow more. In the 1960s, new wheat and rice seeds, the Green Revolution, saved millions from famine. Tractors, fertiliser and irrigation followed. But they came at a price: polluted rivers, lost jobs, and farmers in debt. More food is only half the answer.
visual_style: Overflowing supermarket shelves; a child looking at food through a shop window; citrus being loaded for export; a school feeding scheme serving meals; Norman Borlaug in a wheat field; a centre-pivot irrigator; a green algae bloom on a dam.
pacing: A surprising contrast at the start, then explanation, then a careful ending.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand food security and how science changed farming.
